page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute instance in the High Clock Speed family, operating on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. The instance delivers 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 25 MB of L3 cache. It contains 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance. The instance includes 6 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, zero bundled local storage, and no hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent middle-tier throughput across diverse CPU and memory evaluations. The instance scores in the average tier on Geekbench (1167 single-core, 6841 multi-core) and PassMark CPU (14,861.27), along with balanced single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, synthetic CPU tests show weaker single-core stress performance, and uncached large-block memory write throughput falls into the lower 25% bracket at 24.73 GB/sec. Without AVX-512 extensions, larger modern computational tasks such as 7B parameter LLM inference exhibit lower processing speeds.

Without integrated local NVMe storage, workloads rely entirely on attached cloud block storage. The server maintains a balanced general-purpose resource profile that provides predictable compute performance through dedicated physical core allocations. The configuration suits mid-tier relational databases, Redis caching layers (benchmarked at 12.97 million SET operations per second), static web serving, enterprise application backends, and continuous integration workflows.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the High Clock Speed family, running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor clocked at 3.2 GHz, it supplies 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) and 64.0 GB of RAM. The instance features 6 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, no integrated local storage, and no GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance reliably reaches average performance tiers in PassMark CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and Redis transaction tests, though single-core stress testing and large-block memory write bandwidth remain in the lower quartile. The lack of AVX-512 limits performance in dense modern vector calculations and large-scale model inference. With its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation, ecs.cm4.4xlarge is suitable for static web hosting, general application services, enterprise backend tasks, and medium-scale caching or database workloads relying on external cloud storage.
